title: Exponential-polynomial bound for polynomials
statement: For all $a,d\in\mathbb{N}$, the function $n\mapsto a(n+1)^d$ is exponential-polynomial: there exist $K,k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $a(n+1)^d\le 2^{K(n+1)^k}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
replaced:
For all constants $a, d \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $n \mapsto a(n+1)^d$ is
exponential-polynomial: there exist constants $K, k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$a(n+1)^d \le 2^{K(n+1)^k}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
